# Research: 006-home-gamificada
<!-- Generated by /speckit.plan Phase 0 -->
<!-- Date: 2026-09-16 -->

Built against merged code on `dev` at `d8f0da0`, never against the features' own specs. Citations
are **file plus symbol or section**, never `file:line` — feature 000 lost four citations to line rot.

## The finding that changes the design

**`perfilMaker` cannot be read by an anonymous visitor, and it must not simply be opened.**

`PerfilMaker.ts` § `access` sets `read: scopedAccess()`, and `access.ts` § `scopedAccess` opens
with `if (!user) return false`. So the session client refuses the roster outright to a visitor
with no account.

The anonymous door refuses it too, and its refusal is the designed one. `public-payload.ts` §
`assertPubliclyReadable` admits a collection by exactly three routes — it is in `PUBLISHABLE`
(scoped, with a `status` select that can say `publicado`), or it declares `publicList` in the
scope registry, or it is in `PUBLIC_GLOBAL_CATALOGUE` **and** is `global`. `perfilMaker` is none:
it has no `status`, `scope-registry.ts` § `perfilMaker` declares no `publicList`, and it is scoped.

**And the obvious fix is a data-protection incident.** A `publicList` declaration means *served
unfiltered* — the door's own words. `PerfilMaker.ts` carries `dataNascimento`, `vinculoUnesp`,
`escolaridade`, `curso`, `aceiteTermosEm` and `aceiteTermosVersao`: the personal data 004 collects
under consent at signup step 2. Declaring `publicList` would serve every maker's date of birth,
education and course to any anonymous visitor — the exact leak shape that door's docstring already
names, where `pendingInvites` would have served its invite e-mails.

So FR-031's *"if an operation turns out to have no path through the existing doors, that is a
finding to report with the measurement"* is live, and this is the measurement. See plan § D2 for
what is done about it.

**It is also a live defect on `/ranking` today**, not a new problem: that page reads through
`getTenantScopedPayloadForRSC`, so a signed-out visitor already gets an empty board — *"Ainda sem
makers no ranking"* on a lab that has them. Driven and confirmed: `/ranking` returns 200 signed
out and renders no maker, and renders `Smoke 005 / @smoke005 / 12` with a session cookie.

## Relevant symbols

- `page.tsx` § `HomePage` — **awaits its read in the page function itself**, and the docblock says
  why: *"so the whole tree is resolved before it leaves this function — which is what lets the
  suite call the page and walk what it returns, with no renderer (CLR-003)"*. **Nested async
  components and Suspense are therefore not available to this page**; the concurrency has to
  happen inside `HomePage`.
- `page.tsx` § `lerUltimosProjetos` — the three-way contract every new block copies: `null` is
  *"this read failed"*, `[]` is *"nothing published yet"*, and `TenantUnresolvedError` calls
  `notFound()` for the whole site. The docblock: *"Collapsing the three is how a broken query ends
  up rendering as an empty product."*
- `page.tsx` § `trilhoDeProjetos` — `EmptyState` with `variant="erro"` / `variant="vazio"`, an
  action label and an `href`. The error copy is *"Não foi possível carregar os projetos."*
- `missoes/page.tsx` § `lerMissoes` — reads `missao` through **`getPublicScopedPayloadForRSC`**,
  `depth: 1`, sorted by `titulo`. Missions are public for everyone; the session is never consulted
  for the catalogue itself.
- `missoes/page.tsx` § `estadoPessoal` — returns a four-way union `anonimo | sem-perfil | maker |
  indisponivel`. Two queries: the profile from `usuario`, then the submissions. A failed personal
  read is `indisponivel`, *"one outage costs the personal layer instead of the whole screen"*.
- `missoes/page.tsx` § `submissoesDoMaker` — **one** query, `where: { and: [{ maker }, { missao: { in: ids } }] }`,
  `limit: ids.length` because FR-023's unique index means one row per mission per maker.
- `missoes/page.tsx` § `ETAPAS_POR_ESTADO` — `{ enviada: 1, aprovada: 2, recusada: 0 }`, with
  `satisfies Record<StatusSubmissao, number>` so a fourth review state breaks the typecheck rather
  than rendering 0%. **`recusada` is 0, and the spec's first draft of CLR-003 was wrong about it.**
- `ranking/page.tsx` § `ORDENACAO_DO_RANKING` — `['-xpTotal', 'handle']`, an **array**: the
  comma-joined string is REST-only and orders by nothing on the local API.
- `ranking/page.tsx` § `lerRanking` — `perfilMaker`, no `where` (*"the tenant is the door's, and a
  second opinion here is a second place to get it wrong"*), `depth: 1` so `avatarRender` is art.
- `xp.ts` § `nivelDoLab` — `{ xp, nivel, progresso: { atual, de } }`; empty lab is level 0 with an
  empty bar; throws when the lab has no `regrasXp` row. **Zero callers.**
- `public-payload.ts` § `derivePublishable` — since 005 it asks whether a `status` **select can say
  `publicado`**, not merely whether a field of that name exists.

## Existing patterns and conventions

- **Anonymous reads go through `getPublicScopedPayloadForRSC`; session reads through
  `getTenantScopedPayloadForRSC`.** `/missoes` uses both in one page — the public door for the
  catalogue, the session door for the personal overlay — and that is the shape the Home's band
  copies.
- **A publishable collection gets its `status = publicado` filter from the door**, not from the
  caller. `missao` IS in the publishable set (measured: `artigo, aula, evento, missao, modelo3d,
  projeto`), so a band reading through the public door needs no status clause of its own; one added
  there would be a second expression of a filter the door already applies.
- **Every read catches its own failure and returns `T | null`.** Four pages do it identically.
- **`EmptyState` is the shared surface for both empty and failed**, distinguished by `variant`.
- **Ordering constants are exported and shared**, since 005's ranking defect: *"a literal retyped at
  a second call site is a second ranking free to disagree with this one."*

## Open questions resolved here

- *Does the band need its own `status` filter?* **No, when read through the public door** — the door
  adds it because `missao` is publishable. Yes, if ever read through the session door. Reading the
  catalogue through the public door for everyone keeps one answer.
- *Does `Promise.all` break per-block failure?* Not when the readers never reject. All four already
  catch and return `null`; `Promise.all` over four never-rejecting promises issues them together and
  cannot short-circuit. `allSettled` would also work and is strictly weaker evidence of intent.
- *Can the reads overlap be proven without wall-clock?* Yes — instrument the client and record the
  **order of events**: four `find` calls issued before the first resolves. A timing assertion is
  flaky and is not the proof.
- *Is `missao` in the publishable set?* Yes. `missaoSubmissao` was too, until 005's fix removed it
  by asking whether its `status` can say `publicado` — its vocabulary is `enviada | aprovada |
  recusada`, and the filter threw on the Postgres enum.

## Open questions NOT resolvable from the code

- **The LCP headroom on `/`.** `scripts/lcp-budget.sh` is 2500 ms per page, median of three runs, on
  the 4G profile (1638 kbps). The script owns its preconditions — migrate, seed, build, start — and
  `payload migrate` prompts on a database carrying pushed schema, so it cannot be run against a
  developer's working database at all. Measured on a scratch database instead; see plan § D5. **The
  design does not get to assume the headroom.**
